newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines - March 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines - March 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- SING TAO -- The Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office was given the power to control mainland officials visiting Hong Kong. Vice-ministers would only be allowed to stay in Hong Kong for a maximum of four days.

-- MING PAO -- Independent Legislator Christine Loh had requested to meet officials of the New China News Agency three weeks ago for discussions on the role of the Communist Party in the territory after the handover. But she got no response.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin said the collective authority of the Central Committee should be maintained, and stressed that the Communist Party should have absolute control over the army.
--C hinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said foreign media reports on Hong Kong were incorrect and stressed that Hong Kong would be ruled by Hong kong laws.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES --The housing reforms of China's state enterprises had reached an impasse, and how to enter the housing reforms expenses into the account books remained unclear. Hong Kong financial analysts worried that this would make it impossible for investors to calculate the future profits of listed mainland companies.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- China has improved its prospects of joining the World Trade Organisation by removing two key restrictions in its heavily regulated trade regime.

-- China has issued new rules banning or suspending people found guilty of serious breaches of securities trading ethics from working in the industry in yet another round of tightening since December.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Mainland Chinese officials are compiling lists of candidates for Hong Kong's municipal councils and district boards. A serving urban councillor said he had been approached by one of the officials.
-- China has vowed a hands-off policy towards the first full Special Administrative Region budget, after completing joint preparation of the 97/98 Budget straddling the handover.
